source: RI-STL01 §2 §3 §4 §5 §6, transcribed verbatim. Perception geometry (cones, radii, decay, thresholds) is RI-AI01 §B and is NOT re-opened here.
note_on_units: Every rate is per SECOND in this file and is divided by 60 exactly once, in sim/stealth/detection.js, to reach f@60. Frame figures elsewhere in this piece carry the f@60 suffix per seam S22.

visibility.formula: V = clamp( L^gamma * M * S * E * A , 0.05 , 1.30 )

light_exponent_defect.ruling: RI-STL01 §2 STATES gamma = 0.7 and then publishes a five-row worked table that gamma = 0.7 cannot produce. gamma = 1.36 reproduces all five rows within 0.5%. The worked table is authoritative here and the stated exponent is a transcription defect. AMENDMENT-W1-15-01 files it.

row_4_crouched_unlit_light_Sneak45_cover.note: The item ANNOTATES this row as clamped at the 0.05 floor. At gamma = 0.7 the raw value is 0.0733 and the floor never fires, so the item's own annotation is false at its own stated exponent. This is the decisive tell.

arithmetic.rows_1_and_5: clamped at both exponents; they discriminate nothing.

light_exponent_defect.why_this_direction: gamma > 1 makes darkness matter MORE, which is the direction RI-STL01 §3 argues for in prose ('the lighting artist is a stealth designer') and the direction its DARK-COVERAGE metric assumes. At gamma 0.7 an L = 0.10 floor tile reads as V-multiplier 0.20; at 1.36 it reads 0.044.
light_exponent_defect.how_to_disagree: This value is DATA. Set it to 0.7 here, re-run tools/harness/stl-probe.mjs, and the five worked rows fail instead. Nothing in the code hardcodes it.

cover_A.cover_test: any collider between chest node and eye node for >= 60% of the cone

visibility.never_applies_to_note: Nothing hides you from being hit.

perception_inherited_from_RI_AI01.peripheral_rate_scale_source: RI-AI01 §B row 2: the peripheral cone fills at 0.35x the primary rate. Round 1 shipped 0.45, which is in neither item; RI-STL01 §1 states RI-AI01's perception geometry is NOT re-opened here, so RI-AI01's number stands.
perception_inherited_from_RI_AI01.peripheral_alert_cap_source: RI-AI01 §B row 2 note: the peripheral cone 'cannot exceed alert 70 on its own'.
perception_inherited_from_RI_AI01.hearing_rate_source: RI-AI01 §B hearing rows. RI-STL01 §4 scales the RADIUS of the sphere; RI-AI01 owns the RATE inside it. Flat within the sphere — RI-AI01 gives one number per movement mode and no distance term.

base_fill_conflict_with_RI_AI01.ruling: RI-AI01 §B states the primary sight rate as '100/s at <= 0.5R, 50/s at 1.0R, 0 at > R', i.e. 100 on a plateau then 150 - 100*d/R. RI-STL01 §2's worked table states 97.5/s for V = 1.30 at d = 0.5R, i.e. a base of 75/s at 0.5R. The two are irreconcilable at 0.5R (100 vs 75). This build uses 150*(1 - d/R), which reproduces RI-STL01 §2's five-row table exactly — the table RI-STL01 method 2 asserts against within 5%. The conflict is real, is not the builder's to settle, and is filed as a corpus-coherence defect in AMENDMENT-W1-15-01 §4 for the bar critic.

perception_inherited_from_RI_AI01.base_fill_at_R_note: fill = 150 * V * (1 - d/R) per second in the primary cone; the constant is set so the RI-STL01 §2 worked table reproduces exactly. See sim/stealth/detection.js baseFill().

light_table_L.condition: deep canopy, day (The Hive, Stone Forest)
torchlit interior, within 4 m of a flame
torchlit interior, 4-9 m from a flame

torch.note: L = max(L, 0.80) at all times while carried, and the torch is a hearing-independent alert source at 18 m.

light_falloff.model: inverse-square with a 0.35 m core, summed over sources, clamped to [0,1]
light_falloff.formula: L = clamp( ambient + sum_i( intensity_i / (0.35 + d_i^2) ) , 0, 1 )
light_falloff.note: The renderer and getLightAt() read this same function. RI-STL01's How-we-lose #1 is that light is never sampled at all; sim/stealth/light.js is the answer and getLightAt(x,y,z) is the instrument.

sound.discrete_events_note: None of the four is scaled by Sneak — they are not you moving. The throw is the only offensive stealth tool in the base kit and it directs alert at the impact point, not at you.

sneak_state.input_amendment: AM-W1-15-01 — added to the closed action set in game/src/input/actions.js
sneak_state.blocked_while: any enemy at alert_state == AGGRO within 8 m
sneak_state.blocked_while_note: You may not crouch your way out of an active fight; break line of sight and let RI-AI01's de-aggro run first.
sneak_state.opener_gate_note: RI-PRG03 §6. Deterministic. Below 20 the rear attack is an ordinary light attack that still HITS, because geometry decides hits (S1); it simply is not a critical.

civilian.hearing_suspicion_scale_source: RI-STL01 §6 gives civilians a sight fill and no hearing term at all; RI-AI01 §B gives ENEMIES hearing at 60/40/25 per second. A civilian who reacted to a footfall at an enemy's rate would reach ALARM in 1.67 s of someone sprinting past, which is not a townsperson. 0.35 is this build's declared scale: a sprinting heavy-armoured stranger on dry reed reaches WATCHING in 1.7 s and CHALLENGE in 3.3 s. It is DATA — change it here and nothing in code moves.
civilian.hearing_ceiling_source: A sound makes a townsperson turn round and say something; only SEEING you raises the alarm. Hearing alone is capped at the CHALLENGE threshold, which is RI-STL01 §6's 'last off-ramp' and must stay reachable for a player who was heard and never seen.
civilian.formula: suspicion_fill = base_fill(V, distance, cone) * raceSuspicion[group][race] * contextWeight
civilian.note: Civilians NEVER use the enemy state machine. RI-STL01 How-we-lose: a shopkeeper who enters SUSPICIOUS then AGGRO collapses the whole crime system into combat and destroys the CHALLENGE off-ramp.

worked_rows.label: crouched, unlit, light, Sneak 45, in cover
still, unlit, light, Sneak 100, in cover

permitted_feedback: enemy 18 f@60 head-turn tell at SUSPICIOUS (RI-AI01 T02)
no_meter.rule: AR-2 / ui.hud.minimalism. The correct fix for 'I cannot tell if I am hidden' is more legible darkness and a clearer head-turn tell, never a HUD.

interior_lamps.why: RI-STL01 §3's How-we-lose #1 is 'light is never implemented'. It was implemented — and then, for the whole of wave 1, nothing ever put a light in it outside a scenario. 827 authored interior lamps were DRAWN by render/interior.js and the LightField held zero sources in the running world, so the detection model read the same ambient in a hearth-lit taproom as in a sealed cellar. This block is what turns an authored lamp into an L.
interior_lamps.scale_derivation: The `intensity` on an interiors/*.json lamp is an AUTHORING weight (0.55 oil-lamp, 0.9 or 1.4 hearth), not an L. render/interior.js already rescales it for Three.js (x9 lamp, x22 hearth); the simulation needs its own scale, pinned to RI-STL01 §3's own table rather than to the renderer's. Two rows pin it: 'torchlit interior, within 4 m of a flame' L=0.60 and 'torchlit interior, 4-9 m from a flame' L=0.25 (read at 6 m). With ambient 0.04 and the 0.35 m core those need intensity 9.1560 and 7.6335; the mean is 8.3948. THE FLAME OF THOSE ROWS IS THE ROOM'S FIRE, not a wall sconce, so the mean is divided by the authored hearth weight 0.9 rather than by the oil-lamp's 0.55: 9.3275. A hearth then reads 0.60 at 4 m and 0.27 at 6 m exactly as the item says, and a 0.55 oil-lamp reads 0.39 and 0.20 — dimmer than the room's fire, which is what it is.
interior_lamps.interior_ambient_note: An interior is lit BY ITS LAMPS. Before this, sim/stealth/system.js set defaultAmbient from skyAmbient(env) whenever the player carried no explicit zone — which is the case in every one of the 115 interiors — so a windowless cellar at noon sampled L=1.00 (direct sun) and the same cellar at 03:00 sampled 0.22. Indoors the sky does not reach in; the floor is light_table_L's `unlit` row and every lamp above it is a source.

sleeping_witness.why: RI-CRM01's witness must be someone who was there and could see. The world's NPC schedules (game/data/world/settlements/*.json, activity home|work|tavern|market|errand|watch|street|post) have no `sleep` value at all, so nothing in the build could distinguish a person in their bed from a person standing in their doorway at 03:00 — and a thief robbing a house at night was seen by every resident of it. A person at `home` in these hours is asleep: not a sensor, not an observer, not a witness. It is derived from the schedule the world already publishes rather than authored a second time.

interior_lamps.reach_derivation: RI-STL01 §3's interior rows stop at '4-9 m from a flame'; past 9 m the item's own answer for an interior is the `unlit` row, 0.04. So 9 m is where a flame stops counting, and it is the ITEM's number. A HEARTH is the one fire in the room rather than a fitting on a wall, and gets twice the reach — the same 2:1 the renderer already uses between its hearth and lamp point lights (22 m vs 11 m), so the drawn room and the simulated room agree about which light is the big one. Without a reach the sum over every lamp in a 200 m2 shop clamps 91% of the floor to L=1.00 and the light term stops discriminating anywhere indoors.
interior_lamps.known_divergence_from_the_renderer: render/interior.js caps ILLUMINATING lamps at LIT_CAP=5 per interior and builds the rest as visible but unlit fittings; the simulation lights every deduped lamp. That cap is a rendering budget (591 shadow-casting oil lamps is a slideshow), not a world fact, so it is not copied here — but it means a room with more than five deduped lamps is simulated slightly brighter than it is drawn. Recorded rather than hidden: closing it needs the cap to move into data both files read, and render/interior.js belongs to W1-04.
